survey: A gold five-pointed sheriff star badge, seen almost face-on with a slight tilt, floating on a purple sunburst background. Each of the five points ends in a solid gold ball that is fused cleanly onto the tip. The star body is bevelled, with a raised ridge running from the centre to each point and a raised rim around the edge. A round red cabochon sits in a gold bezel at the centre. No pin or back is visible, which is expected from the front. A floating badge is a normal icon convention, not a support fault. Five ball-tipped points is a real badge form, so the count is fine. The ball tips attach correctly and nothing passes through anything else.

errors.where: Star points, especially the lower-left point
errors.what: The five points are not regular. The lower-left point is clearly shorter and stubbier than the others, and the gaps between points vary. The tilt is too slight to explain this, so the star looks lopsided instead of symmetric like a stamped metal badge.
The red jewel in the centre is an invented part. Real sheriff stars have an engraved or embossed centre seal or lettering, not a gemstone.

fix: A symmetric five-pointed gold sheriff star badge. All five points are the same length and spaced evenly at 72 degrees, and each ends in an identical round gold ball. The centre is a flat round embossed seal with no gemstone.
